ctx.x: Well, when did you eventually leave Cab, then?

I left Cab -- my last engagement was at Birdland, around about February or March or something like that, that was the last. Because we had reorganized again and made the -- after having the four pieces we had raised it back up to a big band again, which we went down to Uruguay, Montevideo, and played all down in there, you know, for the carnival, you know. And so he had had the guys, Doc Cheatham come back, and different guys he had, and Shad and all of them. And Ike, Ike Quebec, and Sam, you know, Sam the man…
Did Ike Quebec and Sam the Man sort of do any battling, you know, like Basie's two tenors, or --

items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: Jonah Jones, he plays one program, every night on his jobs.

ctx.x: Well you see -- I think, you see you take Louis Armstrong, he travelled and he had this small band, and he a set program. That he would play all the time. His program was set. So, at his age, and travelling around, I think he tried to make it as -- he made it as easy on himself as possible by not playing anything other than his program. And when you do that then a lot of things leave you.

You take Jonah Jones is the same way. Jonah Jones, he plays one program, every night on his jobs. So there's 1,000 of things that he has forgotten. And there are many things that I don't say Louis has forgotten, but they just don't play anymore. He'll play the same program year in and year out. Earl Hines the same way. Play the same program -- if you hear Earl today, his program, maybe he'll do the same thing he did last year.
